explanation: This record is the grammatical subject of the claim, which is the shape the vein almost never offers: "The successful implementation of Operation Minden led to the more large scale Operation Commando, which involved a substantial part of I Corps." The article's own lead says the same thing in one word — "Operation Minden was the precursor to the much larger Operation Commando, which established the Jamestown Line." `enabled` and not `caused` because what the article credits is the *successful implementation*: Minden pushed the line nearly five kilometres north of the Imjin and left I Corps standing where the larger advance could be mounted from, which is a thing made possible rather than a thing compelled. `enabled` and not `precondition-of` because the article states a positive "led to" and does not argue that Commando was impossible without it. `probable` and not `consensus` under rule 22 and A2 — the one witness is a Wikipedia record. Both ends are filed under `korean-war`, so this edge is inside an umbrella and does not cross one.
